lines: This is ReproPilot. It turns a bug report into a failing test and a fix, and it runs both before it reports anything.
It was built for the Nebius and NVIDIA hackathon, in the Coding and Agentic Engineering track.
Here is the bundled example. A batching helper called chunked silently drops the last, smaller batch.
Most bug reports look like this. There is a description and a snippet, but no test.
The agent copies the code into a fresh workspace, and a small Nemotron model triages the report.
Then a larger Nemotron model writes a reproduction test, and the test is executed.
The first test is rejected. It imports a module that does not exist, so it fails for the wrong reason.
The agent sends the real error back to the model and asks again.
The second test fails on an assertion that matches the report. Only then is the bug marked as reproduced.
Next comes the patch. Here the fix is a one line change to the range inside chunked.
A patch is kept only if the new test passes and the full suite still passes. All eight tests pass.
The result is a unified diff, the run logs, and a pull request description that is ready to paste.
Model calls go to NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory, through its OpenAI compatible API.
Tests can also run in Token Factory Sandboxes, one isolated virtual machine per run, over the REST API.
One note on this recording. The model answers are scripted fixtures, and the page says so. The test runs are real.
With an API key set, the same flow runs on live Nemotron models. The code is open source under the MIT license.
